meta.promptText: Which vitamin C serum should I buy for dark spots and dull skin in India?

response.text:
If your main goals are **dark spots + dullness**, I’d start with a **10% vitamin C serum**, rather than jumping straight to 20%. Stable vitamin-C derivatives such as **3-O-ethyl ascorbic acid** are generally easier to tolerate, while 10–15% is a practical range for regular use. [www.drsheths.com](https://www.drsheths.com/blogs/skin-care/best-vitamin-c-serum-for-indian-skin-what-actually-works?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.ciplamed.com](https://www.ciplamed.com/-/media/ciplamed/contentmigration/patient-education/pdf/vc201528vitamin20c20serum2920faq20by20patients.pdf?updated=20221212092754&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### My picks in India

### [Minimalist Face Serum]()
*₹629*

### [Plum 15% Vitamin C Face Serum]()
*₹227*

### [Cipla VC15 Serum]()
*₹2,295*

### [Asaya 15% Vitamin C + E & Ferulic Acid Face Serum]()
*₹674*

**🥇 Best overall for most people: Minimalist 10% Vitamin C**  
Good starting point if you haven't used vitamin C before, particularly if you want gradual brightening without an unnecessarily aggressive formula. Current shopping results show it around ₹500–₹630 depending on seller. [www.pingmedoc.com](https://www.pingmedoc.com/pharmacy/buying-guides/best-vitamin-c-serum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**🥈 For stubborn pigmentation / experienced users: Plum 15% Vitamin C**  
A stronger option if you've already tolerated vitamin C well. I wouldn't choose 15% as your first-ever serum if your skin is sensitive.

**🥉 More potent, pharmacy-style option: Cipla VC15**  
Contains **15% L-ascorbic acid**, the most studied form of topical vitamin C. It's a reasonable choice if your skin tolerates acidic vitamin-C products. [www.ciplamed.com](https://www.ciplamed.com/-/media/ciplamed/contentmigration/patient-education/pdf/vc201528vitamin20c20serum2920faq20by20patients.pdf?updated=20221212092754&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### How I'd use it
**Morning:** cleanser → 2–3 drops vitamin C → moisturiser → **SPF 50 sunscreen**.

Sunscreen is crucial: otherwise UV exposure keeps stimulating pigmentation while you're trying to fade it. Visible improvement generally takes **several weeks of consistent use**, not a few days. [www.whowhatwear.com](https://www.whowhatwear.com/beauty/skin/best-products-for-hyperpigmentation?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**My simple recommendation:** If you want me to pick **one bottle**, buy **Minimalist 10% Vitamin C**. If you've already used vitamin C without irritation and your dark spots are particularly stubborn, consider **15%** instead.

If you tell me your **skin type (oily/dry/combination/sensitive)** and roughly your **budget (₹300/₹500/₹1,000+)**, I can narrow it to the best 2–3 options for you.

sources.snippet:
This article from Who What Wear UK provides a comprehensive guide to the best skincare products for treating hyperpigmentation, featuring insights from dermatologists and skin experts. Hyperpigmentation, a common skin concern caused by excess melanin, can result from sun exposure, hormonal changes (such as pregnancy-related melasma), inflammation, or acne scarring. The guide emphasizes that the cause of pigmentation determines the best treatment and underlines the importance of daily SPF use as the most critical step in both prevention and treatment.

Recommended ingredients include vitamin C, niacinamide, azelaic acid, tranexamic acid, and retinoids, which can be found in both over-the-counter and prescription products. Experts caution that results typically take 6 to 12 weeks, or even months, and consistency in skincare is essential.

The article highlights 13 carefully selected products, spanning cleansers, serums, moisturizers, and SPFs. Notable mentions include La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Cleanser, Eucerin Pigment Control SPF50+, The Ordinary Azelaic Acid 10%, and Murad Rapid Dark Spot Correcting Serum. Each product is chosen based on expert input, performance, ingredient quality, and user reviews, providing practical options for anyone tackling dark spots and uneven skin tone.
